claims.statement: Tom Allen returned to St. Louis on 15 August 1874 from the Edwards-Collyer fight near Pittsburg, Pennsylvania.
claims.excerpt: he was to arrive in town yesterday morning

claims.statement: Tom Allen was one of Edwards' seconds in Edwards' fight with Collyer near Pittsburg in August 1874.
claims.excerpt: as he was one of Edwards' seconds, and on the ground

claims.statement: Tom Allen was struck with a rock before the Edwards-Collyer fight but received no damage from it.
claims.excerpt: The champion himself was struck with a rock before the fight, but received no damage from it.

claims.statement: On 15 August 1874 a large crowd gathered all day at Tom Allen's saloon, the Champion's Rest, in St. Louis.
claims.excerpt: the "Champion's Rest" was the scene of an eager multitude all day

claims.statement: On the night of 15 August 1874 Tom Allen kept order among a large crowd at his Free-and-Easy, as was his usual custom when at home.
claims.excerpt: found him seated in the midst of a large crowd, keeping order, as is his usual custom when at home

notes: Allen's own account of the fight is paraphrased by the paper, not quoted. Only Allen's own role and condition are recorded; the fight itself is not his.
